references.text: The first time in the chapter where the disciples describe Jesus' words as hard and unacceptable, which leads directly to Jesus discovering their stubbornness in the next verse.
The consequence of the stubbornness that Jesus discovers in verse 61; many of the disciples withdraw and no longer follow him.
Jesus confirms that he already knew from the beginning who did not believe and who would betray him, underscoring his insight into the disciples' stubbornness.
Jesus warns that the disciples will be scandalized (skandalizō) and abandoned by him, a direct reuse of the term from 6:61 linked to the disciples' reaction to his teaching.
Jesus uses the same word (skandalizō) to describe the one who falls away or is hindered in faith, a central theme in the discussion about the disciples' stubbornness.
